basics.name: Kevin Lacointe
basics.label: Principal Engineer · Elixir, platform & observability
basics.summary:
Principal Engineer with 20+ years building web products, working remotely since 2007.
A team player at heart: I'm happiest hands-on inside a team, building together, mentoring and raising the bar collectively 🤗
First developer at af83 and Welcome to the Jungle, running Elixir in production since 2017, and author of open-source libraries with 800k+ downloads.
I like almost all programming languages and love open source ❤️

work.name: Welcome to the Jungle
work.summary: Cross-team technical lead for the engineering platform: architecture, shared libraries, observability, security and developer experience across ~40 services and several product teams.
highlights: Mentor staff engineers and coach developers on test-driven development.

Led the [Welcome to the Jungle Solutions](https://solutions.welcometothejungle.com/en/) initiative to unify the company's products, with shared client data and a single onboarding across apps: architecture, cross-team coordination and hands-on development.
Set engineering standards through architecture decision records, documentation, CI templates and code review across 40+ repositories; built internal developer tooling.
Adopted AI-assisted development in late 2025 and wrote coding-agent skills that encode the team's conventions.
Created and maintain the shared Elixir libraries used by every backend service.
Led the observability strategy: distributed tracing with OpenTelemetry across ~15 services, centralised error tracking, and monitoring as code.

Led cross-service platform migrations: consolidated messaging on RabbitMQ, standardised HTTP clients and web servers, upgraded legacy Rails applications, and drove dependency security across all services.
Designed and built a third-party ATS integration spanning three products.

work.name: Welcome to the Jungle
work.summary: First developer, alongside a technical PM. Introduced test-driven development, taking the codebase from no tests at all to high test coverage, and mentored the developers who joined in adopting it.
highlights: Bootstrapped the [Welcome Kit ATS](https://solutions.welcometothejungle.com/en/ats) and the [Welcome to the Jungle](https://www.welcometothejungle.com/en) website on Ruby on Rails with React front-ends, then led an early adoption of Elixir (2017) for the website and parts of Welcome Kit.
Welcome Kit: real-time features with ActionCable/AnyCable, and the React/Redux recruiter dashboard with analytics.

[Welcome Originals](https://www.strategies.fr/actualites/marques/4050098W/welcome-to-the-jungle-lance-son-app-de-streaming.html) (2020, since discontinued): owned the Elixir GraphQL API of the video streaming service (DRM playback, encoding pipeline, Apple/Google in-app subscriptions), serving the website, Chromecast and the iOS/Android apps; led the work of the external agency that built the mobile apps.
Started the unification of the products (2021): built the central identity and SSO service shared by all products, with its Elixir SDK (sessions, RabbitMQ events, JSON-schema contracts).
Built supporting services: Algolia-based job alerts, a URL redirector and the deployment CLI.

work.name: af83
work.summary: First developer, in a team of two at the start. Introduced test-driven development, taking projects from no tests at all to high test coverage, and mentored the developers who joined in adopting it.
highlights: Lead developer for large accounts including France Télévisions, SFR, La Poste and RMN-GP, and for many startups.

France Télévisions, 2007 presidential and legislative elections: led the backend and frontend teams building real-time results widgets, results maps and the ingestion of official results (Ruby, JavaScript); load-tested for the results-night traffic peak.
SFR: continued work on [SFR Jeunes Talents](https://www.etonnants-voyageurs.com/Operation-SFR-Jeunes-talents.html), SFR's platform for young creators.

[Francetv info live](https://web.archive.org/web/20160309072848/http://af83.com/work/france-tv-francetv-info-live) widgets: led the team that built the first version of the real-time live-coverage widgets embedded across Francetv pages, where journalists aggregate and publish news from the web and Twitter and reply to readers; started on Rails, then led the move to Go, including the load testing around it.

La Poste, [Digiposte](https://www.laposte.fr/digiposte/tous-mes-documents-partout-et-tout-le-temps): lead developer on the website of La Poste's secure digital document vault, integrated with the Digiposte back-end systems ([af83 case study](https://web.archive.org/web/20130316170657/http://af83.com/work/digiposte)).

RMN-GP, [Images d'Art](https://www.club-innovation-culture.fr/images-dart-500000-images-oeuvres-ministre-fleur-pellerin/): built the Ruby on Rails API behind the platform and led the project with the client, with Elasticsearch powering search and facets over 500,000+ artwork photographs from French museums; launched in 2015 by the French Minister of Culture.
Authored open-source tooling: `zobi` (DRY Rails controllers) and the agency's Capistrano deployment recipes.
